title: SpineRacks and SpinalJ for efficient analysis of neurons in a 3D reference atlas of the mouse spinal cord
protocol: Reconstitute the deeply anesthetized animal with PBS followed by 4% PFA in PBS.
Expose the spinal cord (SC) using standard laminectomy or hydraulic extrusion.
Postfix spinal tissue in 4% PFA in PBS on an orbital shaker for 2–12 hours at 4°C.
Wash SC three times, each for 10 minutes, in PBS on ice.
Remove dura and meninges from the SC.
Transfer SC into a 15 mL tube filled with PBS containing 30% sucrose.
Incubate SC at 4°C for 1–2 days or until the tissue has sunk for cryo-protection.
Prepare a ∼5 cm × 5 cm piece of Parafilm and pour ∼5 mL OCT onto it.
Use the pool of OCT to wash and orient all tissue pieces prior to embedding.
Transfer the spinal cord together with the sucrose solution to a square petri dish.
Cut the spinal cord into three equal parts using sharp spring scissors while viewing under a dissecting microscope.
Cut each piece from step 4 into three equal sized pieces of 3–4 mm.
Gently transfer resulting tissue pieces 1-3 into the OCT puddle with their rostral end facing the top side of the Parafilm square using forceps.
Repeat cutting and transferring process for the other pieces, collecting resulting tissue pieces 4-6 and 7-9 in OCT.
Fill a truncated embedding mold with OCT and mark one side for orientation.
Submerge a SpineRack into OCT and push all the way to the bottom of the mold using forceps.
Release any trapped air bubbles.
Embed tissue immediately within the first 15 minutes after immersing the SpineRack in OCT.
Transfer one tissue piece at a time into the SpineRack.
Load the pieces into wells from top-left to bottom-right in r-c order.
Using forceps, carefully push each tissue piece within a well to the bottom of the mold with its rostral end facing down and the dorsal side facing the marked (top) side of the mold.
Rotate wide cervical segments 1–3 by ∼45° to fit the well.
Leave the mold containing SpineRack and tissue at room temperature for 20–30 min.
Freeze the block on dry ice in a slush of ethanol and crushed dry ice until the block is solid.
Place the tissue block into the cryostat chamber for 20–30 min to allow temperatures to equilibrate.
Mount the tissue block on the block holder in the cryostat with the marked side up and set sectioning thickness to 25 μm.
Section the tissue at approximately -21°C using a Leica Cryostat CM3050S and Sakura Finetec microtome blade.
Section the block and collect all sections continuously on numbered slides.
Collect eight block sections in two rows of four with equal spacing on each slide.
Note the order and orientation of sections on each slide.
Make notes of lost sections, including slide number and position.
Wash slides in a glass Wheaton dish filled with PBS for 5–10 minutes (gentle shaking at room temperature).
Proceed with immunohistochemistry or other staining methods following standard protocols.
Mount slides under coverslips.
Co-stain slides with NeuroTrace or DAPI for subsequent image registration and atlas mapping.
